subject: Logic
title: Regression to the Mean
description: A micro-lesson that makes Regression to the Mean usable.

hook.text: A student scores 98 on a test, then 82 on the next. Did they get worse—or just return to normal?

buildup.text: Regression to the mean says extreme results are often followed by more average ones, simply by chance.

discovery.text: Sports Illustrated's "cover jinx": athletes on the cover often decline afterward. They regressed to the mean.

twist.text: People invent causal explanations—pride, pressure—when the real cause is just statistical inevitability.

climax.text: Beware of judging interventions by what follows an extreme. The bounce-back was going to happen anyway.

punchline.text: Extreme results pull back to average.

quiz.question: What causes regression to the mean?
options: Statistical likelihood of returning to average
